ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, shareholder above 25%, authorized signatory, and every counterparty in the target payment rail must be screened, before onboarding and continuously thereafter, against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) Watchlist, the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and the local adverse public-information and Interpol notices. PEP determination covers foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members and close associates; positive hits require senior-management approval, documented source of wealth and source of funds, ongoing enhanced monitoring, and annual re-review. Negative news and beneficial-ownership complexity must be resolved before execution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (www.iros.go.kr) and National Tax Service Hometax Business Registration Name Search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name must be in Hangul with the mandatory suffix Chusik Hoesa; an English denomination may be registered only as an auxiliary name and cannot replace the statutory Korean name. Transliteration from foreign languages follows the National Institute of Korean Language loanword orthography. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing trade name in the same registration district under Article 23 of the Korean Commercial Act. The four-tier naming structure is: proprietary brand element, industry or business-object descriptor, permissible purpose phrase, and the legal form suffix Chusik Hoesa.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must obtain a written statement of reasons from the registration official. An objection may be filed with the competent registration court within two weeks of receipt, specifying the corrected name or the legal grounds of review. If the objection is denied, an administrative revocation suit under the Administrative Litigation Act may be filed with the competent administrative court within 90 days. During the appeal, the applicant should immediately propose a modified Hangul transliteration and request a preliminary injunction to prevent third-party registration of the substantively similar name while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected for a Chusik Hoesa operating as an M&A advisory boutique. The National Tax Service, registry authorities, and major commercial banks require evidence of a physical registered office with human presence, a dedicated lease, communication infrastructure, and operating records. A commercial mailbox may result in refusal of business registration, bank account denial, and adverse KOFIU or Financial Supervisory Service findings. Shared office space may be acceptable only with a dedicated written lease, on-site management, and documented substance in Korea.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: physical signboard and letterhead, original lease agreement, social insurance and payroll filings, board resolutions and minutes, client engagement files, tax invoices, business license visible on premises, and data and communication equipment. Risk quantified: high; approximately 75% likelihood of an unannounced inspection within the first 18 months, rising to over 90% where reported revenues are inconsistent with lease size, staffing, or advisory transaction volumes. Municipal tax and registry officers may perform field visits without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), in particular Articles 288 through 318 on incorporation and registration, Articles 382 and 393 on the powers of the board of directors, and Article 449 on the adoption of minutes; the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (as amended) for foreign investor status.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office (in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Division), operating the Korean Court Registry portal (www.iros.go.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) together with the Incorporation Registration Application submitted under Article 317 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required under the Commercial Act for a Chusik Hoesa. However, for classification as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investor must invest at least KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 75,000) and such capital must be deposited in a domestic blocked escrow account in the name of the company before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] (CHUSIK HOESA): RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [Company], a Chusik Hoesa organized and existing under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, acting by unanimous written consent in lieu of a formal meeting pursuant to the Articles of Incorporation and the applicable provisions of the Commercial Act, hereby approves the following items effective as of the date of this resolution. 1. Share Capital Subscription and Allocation. The Board acknowledges and accepts the share subscription schedule set forth in the certified Articles of Incorporation executed by the promoters. The Board confirms that the aggregate initial share issuance proceeds have been irrevocably deposited in a blocked escrow account opened for the Company with a Korean commercial bank, and that the bank deposit certificate forms part of the incorporation registration file. The Board allocates one common share for each subscription received and directs the corporate secretary to maintain the securities ledger at the registered office. 2. Banking Facility Authorization. The Board authorizes the President and the Chief Financial Officer, if designated, to open and maintain all corporate bank accounts with the bank maintaining the incorporation escrow. Any disbursement exceeding KRW 10,000,000 shall require the joint approval of two authorized signatories. The bank is instructed to accept signatures of the authorized signatories on all corporate documents, checks, withdrawal orders, and wire transfer instructions. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board fixes the registered head office at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation as filed with the Korean district court. The President is directed to maintain custody of the corporate seal, statutory registers, share ledger, minutes, and financial books at that office, and to give all statutory notices to the National Tax Service and the relevant district court. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [Name] as Chairman of the Board, [Name] as President, and [Name] as Auditor, each to serve until the first annual general meeting. The President shall call the first annual general meeting within three months after the end of the fiscal year to elect or approve the auditor, it being acknowledged that an external auditor will be appointed if the thresholds of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies are met. 5. Seal and Signature. The Board adopts the corporate seal impression submitted with the incorporation application and directs the President to declare the seal to the district court and the tax authority. 6. Delegation and Authority. The Board delegates to the President all powers necessary to complete the incorporation registration, including the payment of registration taxes and court fees, attendance before the court, and submission of all dossiers. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in force until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Article Drafting, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Court Registry portal (www.iros.go.kr) and a licensed Korean notary public under the Notary Public Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoter or its specially appointed legal counsel must first conduct a name availability search on the Korean Court registry portal. If the proposed Korean and English trade name is reserved, the drafter must prepare the Articles of Incorporation specifying the name, purpose, head office location, total authorized shares, issued shares, par value, notification method, and the number of directors and auditors. The Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public under Article 292 of the Commercial Act; the notary shall confirm the promoter identity and the validity of the articles. After notarization, the Articles and the notarization certificate are retained for the court registration filing.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an attorney or agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is denied or queried due to a conflict with an existing registered name, the promoter should submit an alternative name accompanied by a new name search result; the refusal does not suspend the overall formation timeline except for the name-reservation delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Blocked Escrow Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean commercial bank authorized to operate foreign exchange banking business, subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the promoters must open a blocked escrow account at a Korean commercial bank. Each promoter must transfer the agreed subscription proceeds in Korean Won into the account opened under the intended corporate name, and the bank will issue a capital deposit certificate. The certificate must be dated not earlier than the date of the notarization of the Articles of Incorporation, and the deposit amount cannot be withdrawn prior to incorporation except by court order or upon failure of incorporation. The bank issuance fee, if any, is borne by the promoters, and the full amount of the capital must be deposited before the incorporation registration application is submitted to the district court.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application for capital deposit
Source of funds declaration and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the escrow account because of a source-of-funds query, the promoters should provide an internal bank statement, a beneficial ownership declaration, and any prior tax clearance to the bank compliance unit; the deposit certificate will be issued after the bank clears the inquiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the head office, operating through www.iros.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel submits the incorporation registration application to the Commercial Registration Division of the district court. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate issued by the bank, an identification certificate of each promoter, and a foreign nationality certificate whenever a promoter is a non-resident. The court reviews compliance with Articles 317 and 295 of the Commercial Act. If the documents are in order, the court assigns a corporate registration number and registers the company as a legal entity. The company comes into existence on the date of the registration entry pursuant to Article 318. After registration, the court issues a certificate of corporate registration which will be used for subsequent business registration.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Identification certificate or foreign nationality certificate of each promoter
Corporate seal description and signature certificate sampler
Notarized power of attorney to counsel if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order or requests additional evidence, the applicant should file the supplementary documents or apply for a formal correction within two weeks; if the court rejects the application, the promoters may appeal or reapply with a fully cured dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) by way of the Hometax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) with the local tax office governing the head office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after incorporation registration, the company must file for a business registration certificate with the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the head office. The filing must include the corporate registration certificate issued by the court, a copy of the Articles of Incorporation, a lease contract for the registered office, the corporate seal certificate, a statement of capital, and the bank capital deposit certificate. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate containing a unique business registration number and will register the company for corporate income tax and value-added tax duties. Concurrently, the company must subscribe to the Hometax electronic tax invoice service for issued and received tax invoices.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration from the district court
Copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Lease contract of the registered office
Statement of business purpose referencing ISIC 7020
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or queries the business registration, the company should submit a corrected application with the required certificates and pay any assessed late-filing penalty; a certified tax accountant may be retained to expedite the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Bank Accounts, Employment Insurance, and AML Compliance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank, Korea Employment Information Service (KEIS), and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Transactions Report Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As the target business is an M&A advisory boutique, no industrial license is required; however, the company must complete operational compliance before commencing client engagements. The company must open corporate operating bank accounts by presenting the corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, and corporate seal certificate. It must also register with the Korea Employment Information Service for payroll, severance benefits, and compulsory social insurance contributions. If the company will receive client funds or otherwise act as a funds intermediary, it must execute an AML risk assessment and file any suspicious transaction report under the Financial Transactions Report Act with KoFIU. The company should appoint a compliance officer, maintain all client due diligence records for at least five years, and establish a written internal control policy covering conflict of interest, confidentiality, and anti-corruption standards.
required_dossiers: AML policy and risk assessment document
Lease contract and office fire-safety compliance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KoFIU or the bank raises AML concerns, the company should prepare a remedial compliance response, including an updated AML policy, a beneficial ownership schedule, and enhanced due diligence on prospective foreign clients; the account will be activated after the financial institution and KoFIU are satisfied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 7020 is a non-industrial management consulting and M&A advisory service; no factory, chemical, assembly, or warehouse license is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable (the activity is office-based and does not trigger Ministry of Environment permitting)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable: no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation by the M&A advisory operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a physical industrial permit; however, the office must comply with the fire and building safety codes of the National Fire Agency and the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office environments, including installation of fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, and maintenance of an occupied-office safety checklist.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; official electronic portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr). For customs and export clearance, Korea Customs Service (KCS) with UNI-PASS (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Determine Korean VAT and corporate income tax nexus: a non-resident company with a domestic place of business or Korean-source income must register; otherwise it must only appoint a domestic tax representative for withholding obligations. If a Korean fixed establishment or deemed establishment exists, prepare the original certificate of incorporation, articles/certificate of good standing, power of attorney to the Korean tax representative, board resolution appointing the Korean business place manager, lease or proof of place of business, and foreigner identification/passport. Authenticate on HomeTax using an accredited certificate or the Korean tax representative certificate, file the official Business Registration Application under Article 8 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act within 20 days after business commencement, and select the legal form Chusik Hoesa and main business code ISIC 7020. The district tax office with jurisdiction over the Korean place of business will issue the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit business registration number that serves as both the corporate TIN and the VAT ID; the same registration number must be used for VAT e-filing, withholding, and customs export declarations. A non-resident electronic-service supplier without a domestic place of business may instead complete simplified HomeTax registration through a local tax representative before supplying digital services to Korean consumers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Korea; a Chusik Hoesa is always classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at entity level. There is no hybrid mismatch classification election. A qualifying parent with wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries may separately apply for the consolidated group taxation system under the Corporate Tax Act before the start of the group tax year, but that is not a check-the-box mechanism and does not alter the default entity-level taxation of the Chusik Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold; the statutory registration duty arises on the first taxable supply, meaning the threshold is KRW 0. A Chusik Hoesa must obtain a business registration certificate within 20 days after commencing business; the individual simplified taxpayer threshold is irrelevant for a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoices for B2B supplies; e-invoices must be transmitted to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax Electronic Tax Invoice system no later than the following business day. Each e-invoice carries a unique authenticated serial number and electronic signature. B2C cash sales require an electronic cash receipt transmitted through an approved VAN or NTS interface at the point of sale, giving automated daily fiscal reporting. Certified accounting or ERP software must use the HomeTax EDI or API-compatible submission channel. Anti-fraud protection is based on mandatory serialization, system-time stamping in HomeTax, and cross-matching of e-invoices with customs declarations, bank foreign exchange receipts, and VAT returns; there is no separate physical tax stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The zero rate of 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported from Korea after a Korean Customs Service export declaration is accepted and the goods depart Korea; to services supplied to a non-resident where the place of supply or performance is outside Korea and the consideration is received in foreign currency from outside Korea; and to prescribed other foreign-currency-earning transactions for non-residents. For a cross-border M&A advisory boutique, the service contract must specify a non-resident client, the substantive engagement must be performed or consumed overseas, and the fee must be wired into a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank account. If the foreign exchange is not collected within 180 days, the supply is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply at the standard 10% VAT rate unless a statutory exception applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Export Declaration cleared by Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS, evidencing actual export movement for goods)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the consignee, port of loading, and foreign destination
Commercial invoice and packing list issued for the exported goods or services
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Korean foreign exchange bank receipt certificate proving the collection and settlement of overseas payment in foreign currency

For exported services and digital deliverables: signed engagement letter or M&A advisory agreement, delivery or acceptance report, client confirmation that services were used outside Korea, and the foreign exchange remittance receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service compares zero-rated export invoices with UNI-PASS customs data and bank foreign exchange receipts; missing or inconsistent documentation triggers recharacterization of the supply as domestic, with VAT assessed at 10% from the due date plus daily late-payment interest. Additional tax under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act and National Tax Basic Act also applies: 20% of the supply value for issuing a false e-tax invoice, 40% of the underdeclared VAT for intentional fraud, and 10% for negligent underreporting or late filing. Where the 180-day foreign exchange repatriation deadline is missed without approval, the VAT benefit is clawed back. Serious cases are referred for prosecution under the Act on the Punishment of Tax Evaders, and the retroactive assessment period is extended to 10 years for fraudulent or omitted facts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the lead foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS); BOK supervises foreign exchange banks and settlement systems through licensed banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but diligently regulated foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions, including properly documented cross-border advisory fees, are generally convertible through licensed foreign exchange banks without prior approval, subject to transaction documentation and FEIS reporting. Capital account flows are more constrained: inbound equity subscriptions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act require a prior foreign investment report, a temporary investment capital account, and issuance confirmation through a domestic foreign exchange bank; outbound investments, loans, and capital-nature payments above established thresholds require supporting contracts, FEIS declarations, and in some instances MOEF pre-notification. The Korean won is not freely convertible for speculative or round-tripping purposes; foreign exchange banks enforce economic-substance tests, FX position ceilings, and strict beneficiary checks. Profit remittance requires audited financial statements, tax clearance, proof of the source of funds, and a foreign exchange bank remittance receipt; applicable withholding taxes must be settled before dividends or success fees are released. There is no hard surrender ratio on export or service proceeds, but any conversion to KRW must be executed through a licensed foreign exchange bank and declared where required. The practical hurdle is documentation completeness rather than blanket legal restrictiveness, particularly when capital is sourced through layered overseas holding vehicles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory default collection deadline for trade export proceeds is six months from the export declaration date, while service and advisory fees must be collected by the contractual due date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; 100 percent of export proceeds may be retained in a resident foreign currency account, and if converted, the settlement must be made through a licensed foreign exchange bank under FEIS declaration thresholds. Extensions require the handling foreign exchange bank's prior approval with BOK/MOEF notification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and KRW Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and KRW Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and KRW Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account, KRW Operational Account, and USD Foreign Currency Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed foreign exchange banks under FETA and cannot provide KRW settlement, FEIS reporting, capital verification, or compliant official remittance rails for a Chusik Hoesa. Domestic internet-only banks such as Kakaobank and Toss Bank are legal banks but are optimized for retail and are not practical for cross-border M&A advisory treasury, foreign investment capital escrow, trade finance, or multi-currency clearing. The corporate banking mandate must be placed with Tier 1 commercial banks with a fully licensed foreign exchange function; fintech EMIs may serve only peripheral local payroll or operating-expense needs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory rule requiring every director to appear physically in-branch, but in practice the registered statutory representative and at least one signatory must undergo in-person KYC before the account is activated. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the initial corporate account; some banks allow a consular-certified and apostilled power of attorney nominating a local account agent, supported by a notarized board resolution, corporate registration, bylaws, valid passports, and a bank-initiated video conference. For a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa, Korean banks often require a Korean-resident responsible executive or local financial officer to appear in branch for the interview and to receive the security token.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is identified as a non-resident corporate vehicle in a FATF-grey-listed or tax-secrecy jurisdiction, or the direct shareholder is an opaque Chusik Hoesa with nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate register and shareholders' ledger for the immediate and ultimate beneficial owners; standardized UBO declaration identifying all natural persons with 25 percent or more control; audited financial statements for all material upstream vehicles for the last two fiscal years; written legal opinion from an outside securities lawyer confirming no bearer shares, nominee concealment, or PEP concealment; CPA-prepared source-of-wealth report for the founding principals; and bank statements evidencing the lawful origin of the investment capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Success-fee model produces unusual milestone-driven credit surges where inbound M&A client wires do not match revenue forecasts, invoice sequencing, or the entity's small headcount.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letter with fee schedule and success-event definition; board-resolved fee-structure; closing certificate or escrow statement from the relevant M&A transaction; bank statements proving the initial client funds; final tax invoices with VAT and withholding references; internal AML file with a rational risk rating for each counterparty; and a cash-flow projection and business plan demonstrating how middle-market M&A advisory income is earned.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A PEP, close associate of a political figure, or a foreign director appears in the ownership or client chain and authorizes pass-through payments from a client escrow to third-country legal counsel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PEP declaration and beneficial ownership schedule; sanctions and adverse-media screening reports with methodology and date; notarized powers of attorney and corporate authorization for every pass-through payment; underlying transaction history and an independently verified deal calendar; confirmation from the foreign counsel that payments are for legal advice; and an enhanced due diligence file containing FATF/EU jurisdictional risk assessments, direct phone verification with the remitter, and an external forensic accountant's opinion if funds cross a high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming remitter is not the named client, as a wealth fund, holding company, or unrelated third-party payer wires the FDI capital or advisory success fee, triggering misdirection flags under transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written third-party-payer mandate from the commercial client explaining the commercial rationale; certified board resolutions from both payer and beneficiary; contract or side letter naming the third-party payer as settlement agent; KYCC records with the payer's corporate registration, bank confirmation, and source-of-funds; a test-wire schedule and commitment that all future payments will align with the original instruction; and an external legal opinion validating the payment structure under the applicable M&A agreement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: File a foreign investment report with KOTRA or a licensed foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before any transfer, obtaining the FDI report number; open a temporary or escrow foreign investment capital account at the selected Tier 1 bank; route the equity injection as a SWIFT MT103 with the correct beneficiary account, investor name, and FEIS purpose code for subscription of shares; the receiving bank issues a deposit certificate and registers the transaction in FEIS; post-incorporation, the entity converts all or part of the equity to KRW through the domestic FX market and records the conversion in the foreign exchange bank's ledger; an independent auditor performs capital verification using the deposit certificate, corporate registry extract, paid-in-capital statement, and board minutes; shares are then registered, and the Foreign Investment Enterprise Registration is filed to unlock subsequent dividend and liquidation proceeds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use a Tier 1 licensed foreign exchange bank as the clearing agent for all outbound payments. The standard rail is SWIFT MT103 with the correct FEIS outward remittance purpose code, supported by the engagement letter, tax invoice, and milestone certificate. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are available only for underlying goods transactions; for an M&A advisory boutique they should be reserved for financing structures where a success fee or expense reimbursement is embedded in a trade obligation. For USD/KRW activity, clear through the bank's correspondent network, including USD via CHIPS or Fedwire, EUR via TARGET2, and JPY via FXYCS, after conversion at the market rate with proper FEIS reporting; no payments should be routed through unregulated crypto, prepaid, or virtual-card corridors. Large outbound payments of a capital nature require treasury confirmation for FX pricing and may require MOEF declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts in USD/KRW, EUR/KRW, JPY/KRW, and CNY/KRW with a licensed foreign exchange bank, supported by underlying trade or advisory-fee exposure and subject to FETA reporting.
FX swaps and currency rollovers used to manage interim cash-flow timing between the KRW operating account and foreign-currency success fees, with tenor generally not exceeding one year.
Vanilla currency options with physical delivery used to hedge identified deal-specific FX exposure; exotic, barrier, and leveraged options are not permissible.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards are not available to domestic residents without BOK approval; a domestic bank may structure a documented NDF only when the underlying exposure cannot be covered by onshore deliverable forwards and prior regulatory approval has been secured.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM) package: notice of convocation, board-approved financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, statement of retained earnings, statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement), business report, directors remuneration report, external auditor report if applicable, and AGM resolutions approving financial statements and officer compensation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance record maintained at the registered head office and entered in the minute book; not a government filing unless a resolution must be registered with the competent District Court commercial registry, such as the appointment or reappointment of directors, statutory auditor, or audit committee member
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within three months of fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, no later than March 31. Notice to shareholders must be dispatched at least two weeks before the AGM; annual financial statements must be made available for shareholder inspection during the week preceding the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of AGM convening rules exposes responsible directors and officers to an administrative fine for negligence of up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act; failure to register a registrable resolution within two weeks from the resolution date attracts a further fine for negligence and renders the matter unopposable to bona fide third parties; repeated failure to operate and file may lead to NTS business deregistration and court dissolution of an inactive company under Commercial Act Article 520

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax reconciliation schedules, including statutory financial statements and the external auditor report where mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax and the competent district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal-year end; for a calendar-year corporation, by March 31 of the following year. Statutory extension mechanisms may apply, but the tax due remains payable by the original statutory due date unless a permitted deferral is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts an additional tax of 20 percent of the payable corporate income tax; negligent underreporting attracts 10 percent, fraudulent or unjustified underreporting attracts 40 percent, and overdue corporate tax accrues interest at approximately 0.025 percent per day from the statutory due date; if the corporation fails to file returns and conducts no visible business for two consecutive years, the NTS may administratively cancel the business registration and interested parties may petition the court for dissolution under the inactive-company provisions of the Commercial Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local corporate income tax return (local income tax item) and related local surtax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (city, county, or district) through the WeTax local tax e-filing system and the competent regional tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal-year end; for a calendar-year corporation, by April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax penalties mirror the Corporate Tax Act framework: failure to file adds 20 percent of the payable local tax, ordinary underreporting adds 10 percent, unjustified underreporting adds 40 percent, and overdue interest accrues at approximately 0.025 percent per day; continuous nonpayment may result in seizure of bank accounts, receivables, and property, and the local government may deregister the entity for tax enforcement purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified public accountant audit report on statutory financial statements, including the auditors opinion and, where applicable, a written assessment of internal control over financial reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants, the Financial Supervisory Service and DART where the entity is a public-interest company or is otherwise designated for electronic disclosure, and attachment to the corporate income tax return filed with the National Tax Service when an external audit is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit must be completed no later than the date of the AGM and the audit report presented with the financial statements within the three-month AGM window; for a calendar-year corporation the report must be available by March 31; public-interest entities must also satisfy the electronic disclosure deadline under the External Audit Act before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply with the mandatory external audit regime may result in administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, rejection or qualification of financial statements in NTS processing, revocation of tax audit benefits, and enhanced regulatory inspection by the Financial Supervisory Service; the auditor may also face disciplinary sanctions and the company may be deemed to have unfaithful accounting records for tax penalty purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual business report and change reports for foreign shareholding, share transfers, or beneficial ownership events, but only if the Chusik Hoesa qualifies as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through the foreign investment integrated reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report by March 31 of the year following the reporting fiscal year; any change in foreign investment, including acquisition, disposition, transfer of shares, or replacement of the foreign beneficial owner, must be reported within 30 days from the date of such change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or false reporting under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may attract an administrative fine for negligence and may result in revocation or clawback of foreign-investment tax incentives, a formal corrective order, and inability to rely on the foreign-invested enterprise status for regulatory benefits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and corporate secretarial confirmation: audit of the register of members, register of directors, register of statutory auditors or audit committee members, register of charges or mortgages, share transfer ledger, stock option register, and minute book, including reconciliation of the beneficial ownership list with the shareholder register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered head office and corporate secretarial agent; if deficiencies are identified, corrective filings are made with the competent District Court commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the AGM and on a continuing basis; events such as share transfers, director changes, auditor changes, creation or release of charges, and share option entries must be recorded immediately, with court registration of registrable events within two weeks of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or false registers impair the enforceability of share transfers and security interests, block shareholder voting and dividend distributions, and may expose directors to criminal liability and administrative negligence fines under the Commercial Act; failure to register director changes within the two-week window makes those changes unopposable to bona fide third parties and may trigger automatic penalties; serial non-compliance contributes to an adverse corporate standing profile and may be grounds for regulatory strike-off or dissolution proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified public accountant audit is legally required if the Chusik Hoesa meets any of the following thresholds as measured at the preceding fiscal year-end: (1) total assets of at least KRW 12 billion, the principal balance-sheet trigger under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; (2) total assets of at least KRW 5 billion but less than KRW 12 billion where the company also meets the current Presidential Decree gates for employee headcount and revenue, currently applicable where average full-time employees equal or exceed 100 or annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion; (3) listed status or designation as a public-interest entity under the External Audit Act irrespective of asset size; (4) an order or designation by the Securities and Futures Commission requiring external audit; or (5) an express election in the articles of incorporation or an extraordinary shareholders resolution to appoint an external auditor. Smaller companies below the mandatory threshold must still appoint a statutory auditor or audit committee to review the financial statements for the AGM
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed and public-interest entities must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). Unlisted private Chusik Hoesa may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, or may adopt K-IFRS voluntarily, provided the chosen framework is applied consistently. All statutory audits must comply with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, the Korean Auditing Standards, and the accounting framework selected by the company, with group consolidated financial statements prepared under K-IFRS where applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Chusik Hoesa must maintain a current register of members at its registered head office or registered transfer agent. Any share transfer, pledge, or beneficial ownership change must be recorded in the register without delay; until recorded, the change is not effective against the company. There is no standalone national UBO annual filing for a private unlisted Korean corporation, but the entity must perform an annual internal confirmation before the AGM reconciling the register of members, the share transfer ledger, and the list of beneficial owners, and must respond to banking counterparty AML beneficial-owner identification requests. If the entity is registered as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any change in foreign shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reported to KOTRA and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy within 30 days of the change, in addition to the annual foreign-invested enterprise business report due by March 31
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditor and Audit Committee Members
Register of Share Transfers and Pledges
Stock Option Register (if shares or options are issued)
Minute Book of Shareholder and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 to USD 3,500 per annum in Seoul and the Incheon business corridor; USD 700 to USD 2,500 per annum in other provinces, depending on registered-office address, registered-agent services, and corporate secretarial support scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 25,000 for a small or mid-size private M&A advisory boutique; USD 25,000 to USD 80,000 or more for a consolidated, K-IFRS, foreign-invested, or multi-jurisdictional Chusik Hoesa requiring additional group audit work and cross-border transaction testing

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top statutory national corporate income tax rate under the progressive 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% brackets of Article 55 of the Corporate Tax Act; plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax due, yielding a 26.4% aggregate top effective burden for non-resident shareholders and domestic entities
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays of 100% exemption for 5 years and 50% exemption for a further 2 years for qualifying foreign-invested entities; Tax Incentive Limitation Law R&D expense tax credits up to 40%; self-developed patent and IP income eligible for an effective 5% patent box rate; M&A advisory boutiques generally cannot rely on sectoral holidays unless they maintain real employees, premises, and Core Income-Generating Activities inside a designated Free Economic Zone

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return for Tax Base and Imputation under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, electronically filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr, with statutory supporting schedules covering balance sheet, income statement, tax adjustment statements, foreign transaction schedule, foreign tax credit schedule, and transfer pricing disclosure
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File no later than the last day of the third month following the close of the fiscal year, for example by 31 March for a 31 December year-end; if the deadline falls on a weekend or public holiday it is extended to the next business day; a one-month extension is available when the final return is prepared and signed by a Korean certified public accountant or tax attorney

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, domestic business place, fiscal year, representative director, share register, and non-resident shareholder information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every non-resident shareholder, TIN, Tax Residency Certificate jurisdiction, country of residence, and ownership percentage; failure to identify the ultimate non-resident shareholder creates dividend WHT, CRS, and beneficial ownership nonconformity; attach board resolutions proving the foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa has valid corporate existence and representative authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and gross sales from M&A retainer fees, deal success fees, break-fee income, project management fees, annual advisory retainers, and SWIFT/wire settlement proceeds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue earned from Korean-sourced business on a gross basis, including success fees for cross-border deals managed by the Korean office; do not net out success-fee sharing paid to foreign consultants; revenue allocated to an offshore related party without real staff, delivery functions, and client relationships in that offshore office will be recharacterized as Korean revenue; translate foreign-currency receipts using the Bank of Korea daily rate and attach the invoice ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and deductible expenses: payroll, data subscriptions, legal and due-diligence counsel, valuation software, rent, depreciation, travel, insurance, and professional indemnity costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign related parties are deductible only if evidenced by written agreements, actual deliverables, time records, and an arm's length transfer pricing analysis; amounts paid to low-tax shell companies without office premises, employees, or deal functions are non-deductible and may trigger withholding obligations; statutory entertainment expense caps must be applied and any excess added back to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating income and ordinary income from statutory books, including profit or loss from domestic and foreign activities after allocation to a Korean permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean PE of a non-resident enterprise, allocate only income attributable to the Korean office under the OECD business profits attribution rules and the applicable DTA; M&A advisory income is recognized when the service is performed and the close occurs; stage-of-completion revenue on incomplete mandates must be booked per Korean GAAP/IFRS; all global cross-border deal revenue must be supported by contemporaneous staffing, meeting, tax invoice, and execution evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: add-backs of non-deductible expenses such as fines, penalties, statutory excess entertainment, and certain capital losses; deduction of tax-exempt income, foreign-source income exclusion, and net operating loss carryforward within the statutory framework of this filing schema
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the loss carryforward statement for every prior year and for any merged advisory predecessor; preserve continuity of ownership and the actual M&A advisory business before using the 5-year loss carryforward; a liquidation/reincorporation designed only to revive expired losses will be denied under the general anti-abuse rule; loss carryforward usage must not produce a tax base inconsistent with the arm-length financial results of the Korean boutique.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base and tax calculation: application of progressive national tax brackets, local income tax surtax, interim prepayments, foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, other tax credits, and final net tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute foreign tax credit separately on a country-by-country basis with original foreign tax withholding certificates and proof of actual payment; no credit is allowed for tax paid by a shell or conduit; transfer pricing adjustments made in prior examinations must be included in the reconciliation; attach the schedule showing the 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% progressive brackets plus the 10% local surtax on the national corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding reconciliation: dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, and treaty-relief claims in respect of every remittance to non-resident shareholders, lenders, licensors, and foreign service providers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each outbound remittance separately: gross payment, statutory Korean WHT, treaty rate, DTA article relied upon, Tax Residency Certificate date and number, and beneficial ownership evidence; if treaty relief is claimed and later rejected, additional tax, daily interest, and penalties run from the original remittance date; the withholding agent must file the prescribed tax treaty exemption application through HomeTax within the statutory withholding payment window; a non-resident not actually the beneficial owner of the fee cannot claim a reduced DTA rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure: intercompany services, management fees, success-fee sharing with foreign affiliates, royalties, interest on shareholder loans, cost allocations, and M&A advisory referral fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the International Transactions Schedule, state the transaction amount in KRW, identify the foreign related party, select the Most Appropriate Method, provide the arm's-length range and comparable data, and explain why TNMM or another method fits the strategy of a middle-market cross-border M&A advisor; prepare and retain the Local File when cross-border intercompany transactions reach the KRW 10 billion threshold; failure to file TP disclosure converts the taxpayer's burden of proof and exposes the entity to penalty adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without just cause triggers additional tax equal to 20% of the underpaid national corporate tax, reduced only in limited circumstances for returns filed within one month; negligent underreporting attracts 10% of the underpaid tax, fraudulent omission or false invoices attract 40%; daily delinquency interest at the statutory rate of approximately 0.022% per day runs until full payment; failure to submit transfer pricing documentation adds a further 10% to 20% penalty; criminal tax evasion involving intentional concealment can lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years, a fine of up to KRW 100 million, and disqualification from Korean financial-sector licensing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national dividend withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax, for a 22% aggregate withholding tax rate on outbound dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to non-resident shareholders when no treaty relief applies
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the foreign beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence country for the relevant year, execute a beneficial ownership certificate confirming that no nominee, agent, conduit, or shell entity stands between it and the Korean payer, and file the prescribed Application for Tax Exemption or Reduction under a Tax Treaty with the Korean withholding agent before remittance; the withholding agent must submit the application through HomeTax and maintain contemporaneous evidence of effective tax residence, real business activities, and ownership structure; if the taxpayer fails to apply before remittance, a refund claim may be made through an amended withholding return within 3 years subject to statutory interest, but Korean authorities will deny relief for mailbox companies lacking substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest on intercompany debt and royalties for brand, software, or deal-origination intellectual property are subject to the statutory 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax, aggregating 22% absent a treaty; Korean DTA reduced rates commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and 5% to 15% for royalties, but only where the recipient is the true beneficial owner and where Korean thin-capitalization rules do not recharacterize excessive interest as a dividend under the 3:1 debt-to-equity limitation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border intercompany transactions between the Korean entity and foreign related parties aggregating KRW 10 billion or more in a business year require Local File preparation; a Master File is additional required where the Korean entity belongs to a multinational enterprise with group-wide consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more; the Korean entity must also file the statutory international transaction summary in the corporate return whenever the statutory reporting floor is exceeded.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not impose a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations label, but the Core Income-Generating Activities doctrine is enforced through the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17 general anti-abuse rule, the International Tax Coordination Law Articles 6 and 61, OECD MLI principles, and Supreme Court substance-over-form precedent; for this M&A advisory boutique, the CIGA are deal sourcing, financial modeling, negotiation, due diligence, execution, and post-closing advisory; those activities must be performed through real Korean employees, premises, active management, contracts, and bookkeeping in Korea, and any booking of revenue or success fees to a Cayman, Singapore, Hong Kong, or Delaware shell with no actual staff or strategic control will be disregarded and the income re-attributed to Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Under-Filing of Corporate Income Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The representative director intentionally omits KRW 8 billion of closing success fees from Box 2, registers fictitious advisory invoices from a related offshore shell entity, and files no Corporate Tax Return for two consecutive fiscal years based on a false claim that the Korean office was dormant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraudulent omission attracts an additional tax of 40% of underpaid tax plus statutory daily interest; under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, the responsible person is subject to imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million; the tax authority may also revoke the company's statutory M&A advisory license and disqualify it from participating in regulated cross-border deal structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director's personal assets may be collected under National Tax Collection Act Article 39 secondary liability for unpaid corporate taxes, and the director is jointly liable for restitution to the company and third parties under Commercial Act Article 401; the director may be placed on the National Tax Service delinquent-payer blacklist, subjected to a departure ban, and held personally liable for civil restitution of the diverted success-fee amount in addition to criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Fraud on Outbound Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa remits USD 30 million to its non-resident parent as a purported intercompany loan repayment through SWIFT while the payment is in substance an undeclared dividend; no 22% aggregate withholding tax is remitted, no Tax Residency Certificate is obtained, and no tax treaty relief application is filed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company remains liable for the full 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local surtax; additional withholding penalties of 10% or 20% apply for negligent versus fraudulent failure, together with daily interest; the payment is recharacterized as a dividend and no interest deduction or offset is available.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director is personally liable for remitting withheld taxes under National Tax Collection Act Article 41, with personal bank accounts and assets subject to seizure; the director is blacklisted, can be prevented from leaving Korea, and may face criminal punishment where the non-remittance is fraudulent or grossly negligent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Shell Arrangement Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean M&A boutique invoices KRW 25 billion in closing success fees to a Delaware LLC controlled by the same shareholders; the Delaware entity has no employees, no office, no valuation capability, and no due-diligence staff, and the Korean entity then receives only 20% of the fee through a 'management rebate,' shifting KRW 20 billion of Korean-source profit offshore; no intercompany agreement, comparability study, or Local File is prepared even though the transaction far exceeds the KRW 10 billion reporting threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority recomputes taxable income using an arm's-length method such as TNMM or Profit Split under Article 5 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs; the adjustment adds 10% penalty on the understated tax, daily interest, and a separate transfer-pricing documentation penalty; the general anti-abuse rule disregards the Delaware shell and attributes the entire success fee to the Korean entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly executed the bogus management-rebate arrangement are personally liable for the assessed tax under National Tax Collection Act Article 39, and can be sued for breach of fiduciary duty under Commercial Act Article 401; personal assets funded from the shifted fees must be disgorged; the directors face criminal imprisonment and travel blacklisting where the shell arrangement is proven to be fraudulent, and they cannot invoke the corporate veil to protect personal estates.
